records.definition: One provider-neutral contract implemented by multiple database/provider-specific routes.
Declared technology category such as OOREXX_NATIVE, FOREIGN_RUNTIME or PROCESS_BRIDGE.
A machine-readable statement that an implementation can perform a named behavior, with explicit status.
A separately published boundary/constraint explaining what an implementation cannot or does not yet do.
Capability is implemented and eligible subject to requirements/policy.
Capability is explicitly absent and makes a hard requirement ineligible.
Capability may exist only under extra conditions and is not treated as satisfied without those conditions.
Capability state is not established; never treated as implicit support.
Planner output describing eligibility and rejection reasons such as UNAVAILABLE, FAMILY_MISMATCH or MISSING_CAPABILITY:name.
Binding an acquired session/transaction to one selected backend implementation for its lifetime.
A separately declared alternative implementation selected only at a safe pre-acquisition boundary.
Provider-neutral NativeDatabaseExecution/Result/Column/Row preserving provider metadata and SQL NULL without mandatory text flattening.
Adapter that renders structured results into an older Database Core text/tabular framing without redefining native result semantics.
The pure-ooRexx GeoPackage direct reader that works cross-platform without external GIS/sqlite libraries.
Future optional Foreign Runtime sqlite3/spatial implementation providing speed/pushdown while leaving portable ooRexx correctness path intact.
Future client-side MySQL/MariaDB native connector belonging to this backend family.
Separate inbound MySQL/MariaDB classic-wire compatibility server in front of NoSQLServer; not the outbound MySQL backend.
Executed evidence that a specific component/version/companion set satisfies claimed behavior; availability alone is not qualification.
Explicitly published capability absence or unimplemented feature retained as evidence until implementation and qualification exist.
Direct implementation route from ooRexx perspective; may be pure ooRexx or Foreign Runtime and must not be assumed to mean FFI.
